Rows: 7,673 fields in "Field-level main data"; 6,481 with Status "operating", of which 426 have no Latitude/Longitude (left out).

Production: "Field-level production data", each fuel's newest Data Year, in GEM's converted units (the detail column, as GEM gives them). The capacity column is their total in million barrels of oil equivalent a year (boe): oil, condensate and NGL in million bbl/y as they are, gas at 6,000 cubic feet per boe (1 million m³ = 0.0058858 million boe), GEM's own million boe/y as given. The years differ between fields.

P3-9 cap: 6,055 operating fields with coordinates, over the 5,000 markers a layer draws, so the fields GEM reports producing less than a threshold are left out (ruling R23), the threshold starting at 0.1 million boe/y and raised in steps of 0.1: at 0.2 million boe/y, 1,122 fields are left out and 4,933 remain, 653 of them with no field-level production figure (kept: some of the largest are reported only at project level).

Check: largest fields: Burgan Oil and Gas Field (Kuwait) (KWT) hydrocarbons 620 million boe/y (2023); Rumaila Oil Field (Iraq) (IRQ) oil 518 million bbl/y (2022); Tupi Oil and Gas Field (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil) (BRA) gas 15,009 million m³/y, oil 299 million bbl/y (2024); Shaybah Oil and Gas Field (Saudi Arabia) (SAU) gas 45.5 million m³/y, oil 365 million bbl/y (2023); Spraberry (Trend Area) - Pioneer Natural Res. Usa, (Unconventional) Oil and Gas Asset (Texas, United States) (USA) NGL 70 million bbl/y, gas 16,801 million m³/y, oil and condensate 182 million bbl/y (2024).
Published: GEM names the release month only; 2026-03-01 stands for March 2026 and is never shown as a day.
